components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Explore how water moves continuously through Earth's atmosphere, land, and oceans.

components.title: Evaporation and Transpiration
components.body: Heat from the sun warms water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, causing it to evaporate into water vapor. Plants also release moisture from their leaves through a process called transpiration.

components.title: Condensation and Cloud Formation
components.body: As warm water vapor rises high into the atmosphere, it cools down and turns back into tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals. These droplets gather around microscopic particles in the air to form clouds and fog.

components.title: Precipitation and Collection
components.body: When the water droplets in clouds become too heavy to remain suspended in the air, they fall back to Earth as precipitation—rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This water collects in oceans, rivers, and underground aquifers, ready to begin the cycle again.

components.title: Worked Example: A Puddle on a Sunny Day
components.body:
Imagine a rainwater puddle sitting on a warm sidewalk after a storm.

`Observation:` Over a few hours, the puddle slowly shrinks and eventually disappears entirely.

`Explanation:` Solar energy transfers heat to the liquid water, increasing molecular motion until water molecules escape into the air as invisible vapor (evaporation).

questions.question: What process describes plants releasing moisture from their leaves into the atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the process where plants absorb water through their roots and release water vapor through pores in their leaves.

questions.question: What causes water vapor to turn into clouds during the condensation stage?
options: Cooling down high in the atmosphere
Freezing completely into solid ice blocks
questions.explanation: As warm water vapor rises, it encounters colder temperatures aloft, causing it to cool and condense into liquid droplets.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a form of precipitation?
questions.explanation: Evaporation is the process of liquid turning into vapor, which is the opposite of precipitation (water falling from clouds).
